# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

122	  const _StreamingCursor();
123	
124	  @override
125	  State<_StreamingCursor> createState() => _StreamingCursorState();
126	}
127	
128	class _StreamingCursorState extends State<_StreamingCursor> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
129	  late final AnimationController _controller = AnimationController(
130	    vsync: this,
131	    duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 1000),
132	  )..repeat();
133	
134	  @override
135	  void dispose() {
136	    _controller.dispose();
137	    super.dispose();
138	  }
139	
140	  @override
141	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
142	    return AnimatedBuilder(
143	      animation: _controller,
144	      builder: (context, _) {
145	        final opacity = 0.2 + 0.8 * (1 - (_controller.value - 0.5).abs() * 2).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
146	        return Opacity(
147	          opacity: opacity,
148	          child: Container(

151	            margin: const EdgeInsets.only(left: 2),
152	            color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary,
153	          ),
154	        );
155	      },
156	    );
157	  }
158	}

1	import 'dart:convert';
2	
3	import 'package:cerne/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart';
4	import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
5	
6	/// On-device, cross-restart persistence for the entries the user has
7	/// already seen (the PRD's "local read cache" — requirements.md line 50/125:
8	/// results from it stay visible offline and reconcile with the server on
9	/// reconnect, with no duplicates). Keychain-backed, same pattern as
10	/// `VaultSecureStorage` — journal content is personal data, so it stays
11	/// encrypted at rest like the PIN it already sits behind.
12	///
13	/// Distinct from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s in-memory `cachedEntries`: that
14	/// field only ever held optimistic just-created entries for this process's
15	/// lifetime (research.md R8, 003-multimodal-capture). This class is what
16	/// makes that same list survive an app restart, which is what a cold open
17	/// on an already-offline device needs (closing snapshot at unit completion
18	/// did not cover this path — see Meus Registros intervention report).
19	class EntriesLocalCache {
20	  EntriesLocalCache({FlutterSecureStorage? storage})
21	    : _storage = storage ?? const FlutterSecureStorage();
22	
23	  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;
24	
25	  static const _key = 'entriesLocalCache';
26	
27	  Future<List<Entry>> readAll() async {
28	    final raw = await _storage.read(key: _key);
29	    if (raw == null) return const [];
30	    try {
31	      final decoded = jsonDecode(raw) as List<dynamic>;
32	      return decoded.map((e) => _fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList();
33	    } on FormatException {
34	      return const [];
35	    } on TypeError {
36	      return const [];
37	    }
38	  }
39	
40	  Future<void> writeAll(List<Entry> entries) {
41	    final encoded = jsonEncode(entries.map(_toJson).toList());
42	    return _storage.write(key: _key, value: encoded);
43	  }
44	
45	  Map<String, dynamic> _toJson(Entry e) => {
46	    'id': e.id,
47	    'content': e.content,
48	    'source': e.source.name,
49	    'chatMessageId': e.chatMessageId,
50	    'occurredAt': e.occurredAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
51	    'tags': [
52	      for (final tag in e.tags) {'id': tag.id, 'name': tag.name},
53	    ],
54	    'piiStatus': e.piiStatus.name,
55	    'piiSpans': [
56	      for (final span in e.piiSpans)
57	        {'start': span.start, 'end': span.end, 'type': span.type},
58	    ],
59	    'embeddingStatus': e.embeddingStatus.name,
60	    'mediaDurationSeconds': e.mediaDurationSeconds,
61	    'serverRevision': e.serverRevision,
62	    'createdAt': e.createdAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
63	    'updatedAt': e.updatedAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
64	    'similarity': e.similarity,
65	  };
66	
67	  Entry _fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> data) => Entry(
68	    id: data['id'] as String,
69	    content: data['content'] as String,
70	    source: EntrySource.values.byName(data['source'] as String),
71	    chatMessageId: data['chatMessageId'] as String?,
72	    occurredAt: DateTime.parse(data['occurredAt'] as String),
73	    tags: (data['tags'] as List<dynamic>)
74	        .map(
75	          (t) => EntryTag(
76	            id: (t as Map<String, dynamic>)['id'] as String,
77	            name: t['name'] as String,
78	          ),
79	        )
80	        .toList(),
81	    piiStatus: PiiStatus.values.byName(data['piiStatus'] as String),
82	    piiSpans: (data['piiSpans'] as List<dynamic>)
83	        .map(
84	          (s) => PiiSpan(
85	            start: (s as Map<String, dynamic>)['start'] as int,
86	            end: s['end'] as int,
87	            type: s['type'] as String,
88	          ),
89	        )
90	        .toList(),
91	    embeddingStatus: EmbeddingStatus.values.byName(
92	      data['embeddingStatus'] as String,
93	    ),
94	    mediaDurationSeconds: data['mediaDurationSeconds'] as int?,
95	    serverRevision: data['serverRevision'] as int,
96	    createdAt: DateTime.parse(data['createdAt'] as String),
97	    updatedAt: DateTime.parse(data['updatedAt'] as String),
98	    similarity: (data['similarity'] as num?)?.toDouble(),
99	  );
100	}

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	**Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's extension
4	hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)
5	
6	**Date**: 2026-10-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
7	
8	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md` §1
9	(RF04), §6.3 (`chat-sessions-create`/`chat-sessions-list`/`chat-messages-list`/`chat-messages-send`/
10	`chat-messages-retry`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §10 (no new fixed parameter for this unit),
11	§13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/chat/sessions*` schemas; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
12	`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §§2.2
13	("Tela 1 — Home/Chat", "Tela 3 — Menu lateral"), 3, 4, 6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on
14	F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`) and RF03 (`specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/`), both already implemented — this
15	is the unit that makes Home/Chat's currently-inert, fully-disabled composer (F000's own scaffold,
16	`home_chat_shell_page.dart`) and the side menu's currently-static `AppDrawer` actually work.
17	
18	## Summary
19	
20	Home/Chat gains a live, persisted conversation with the backend's RAG-grounded agent
21	(`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`, SSE: `message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`), and the side
22	menu's `AppDrawer` gains a paginated, offline-cached "CONVERSAS" list (`GET /chat/sessions`) plus a working
23	"Novo Chat" action. A new feature folder, `lib/features/chat/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
24	`ChatSession`/`ChatMessage`/`ChatSessionsPage`/`ChatStreamEvent`/`ChatTitleDeriver` (domain), `ChatRemoteDataSource`/
25	`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` (data), and two blocs — `ChatBloc` (the one live conversation: streaming,
26	retry, lazy session creation, composer gating) and `ChatSessionsBloc` (the side menu's own paginated list,
27	mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s RF07-established shape almost exactly, research.md R7). `core/network/ApiClient`
28	gains one new, chat-agnostic method, `sseStream()`, built on `dio`'s own `ResponseType.stream` with a
29	hand-rolled SSE frame parser (research.md R1) — no new package. `core/network/ConnectivityChecker` gains a
30	live `onConnectivityChanged` stream (research.md R8), layered on top of (not replacing) the existing
31	synchronous `hasConnection()` pre-check every write path in this app already uses. A new, Keychain-backed
32	`ChatLocalCache` (mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own pattern) persists the session list, each individually-
33	opened session's message history, and the last-active session id, satisfying spec.md's Clarification 3
34	(offline browsing covers every previously-opened conversation, not just the one open at disconnect) and its
35	own Assumptions (resuming the last conversation on app restart). A new chat message or its own session is
36	never created eagerly — only lazily, at the moment a first message is actually sent (FR-010) — and the title
37	sent with that creation call is derived client-side from the message's own text by a new, pure
38	`ChatTitleDeriver` (research.md R6), since the backend has no auto-titling or rename endpoint of its own. No
39	new `go_router` route is added: Home/Chat stays the one existing, unparameterized `/home` screen, swapping its
40	displayed conversation in place via the two blocs it's now provided with (research.md R7) — "Novo Chat" and
41	selecting a past conversation from the drawer are both in-place state transitions, not navigations.
42	
43	## Technical Context
44	
45	**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
46	F000/RF01/RF02/RF03/RF06/RF07.
47	
48	**Primary Dependencies**: No additions. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
49	`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `sseStream()`), `go_router` (no new route), `flutter_secure_storage`
50	(for the new `ChatLocalCache`), `connectivity_plus` (its own `onConnectivityChanged` stream, previously
51	unused — `ConnectivityChecker` only ever called `checkConnectivity()` once per check before this unit); dev-only
52	`mocktail`, `bloc_test`. SSE is consumed via a ~30-line hand-rolled parser over `dio`'s existing byte-stream
53	support, explicitly chosen over any third-party SSE package (research.md R1) — the OpenAPI contract's own
54	schema for both SSE operations is `content: text/event-stream` / `{type: string}`, i.e. genuinely no typed
55	shape to generate a client from.
56	
57	**Storage**: One new on-device store, `ChatLocalCache` (research.md R4) — three independent
58	`flutter_secure_storage` keys (`chatSessionsLocalCache`, `chatMessagesLocalCache`, `chatLastActiveSessionId`),
59	same Keychain-backed, JSON-encoded mechanism `EntriesLocalCache` (RF01) already established for personal
60	content. No local database, no new third-party persistence package.
61	
62	**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via
63	`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
64	`chat_title_deriver.dart` (pure), `ChatMessage`'s status-transition shape, `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s
65	silent-refresh-and-retry branches (both the non-streaming shape reused verbatim from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`,
66	and the new first-frame-only streaming variant, research.md R3), and `ApiClient.sseStream()`'s own frame
67	parser (a `core/` addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `error_mapper_test.dart`/similar already
68	live). `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` and `domain_purity_test.dart` both run unmodified against the new

# Implementation Plan: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's extension
hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md` §1
(RF04), §6.3 (`chat-sessions-create`/`chat-sessions-list`/`chat-messages-list`/`chat-messages-send`/
`chat-messages-retry`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §10 (no new fixed parameter for this unit),
§13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/chat/sessions*` schemas; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §§2.2
("Tela 1 — Home/Chat", "Tela 3 — Menu lateral"), 3, 4, 6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on
F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`) and RF03 (`specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/`), both already implemented — this
is the unit that makes Home/Chat's currently-inert, fully-disabled composer (F000's own scaffold,
`home_chat_shell_page.dart`) and the side menu's currently-static `AppDrawer` actually work.

## Summary

Home/Chat gains a live, persisted conversation with the backend's RAG-grounded agent
(`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`, SSE: `message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`), and the side
menu's `AppDrawer` gains a paginated, offline-cached "CONVERSAS" list (`GET /chat/sessions`) plus a working
"Novo Chat" action. A new feature folder, `lib/features/chat/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
`ChatSession`/`ChatMessage`/`ChatSessionsPage`/`ChatStreamEvent`/`ChatTitleDeriver` (domain), `ChatRemoteDataSource`/
`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` (data), and two blocs — `ChatBloc` (the one live conversation: streaming,
retry, lazy session creation, composer gating) and `ChatSessionsBloc` (the side menu's own paginated list,
mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s RF07-established shape almost exactly, research.md R7). `core/network/ApiClient`
gains one new, chat-agnostic method, `sseStream()`, built on `dio`'s own `ResponseType.stream` with a
hand-rolled SSE frame parser (research.md R1) — no new package. `core/network/ConnectivityChecker` gains a
live `onConnectivityChanged` stream (research.md R8), layered on top of (not replacing) the existing
synchronous `hasConnection()` pre-check every write path in this app already uses. A new, Keychain-backed
`ChatLocalCache` (mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own pattern) persists the session list, each individually-
opened session's message history, and the last-active session id, satisfying spec.md's Clarification 3
(offline browsing covers every previously-opened conversation, not just the one open at disconnect) and its
own Assumptions (resuming the last conversation on app restart). A new chat message or its own session is
never created eagerly — only lazily, at the moment a first message is actually sent (FR-010) — and the title
sent with that creation call is derived client-side from the message's own text by a new, pure
`ChatTitleDeriver` (research.md R6), since the backend has no auto-titling or rename endpoint of its own. No
new `go_router` route is added: Home/Chat stays the one existing, unparameterized `/home` screen, swapping its
displayed conversation in place via the two blocs it's now provided with (research.md R7) — "Novo Chat" and
selecting a past conversation from the drawer are both in-place state transitions, not navigations.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000/RF01/RF02/RF03/RF06/RF07.

**Primary Dependencies**: No additions. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `sseStream()`), `go_router` (no new route), `flutter_secure_storage`
(for the new `ChatLocalCache`), `connectivity_plus` (its own `onConnectivityChanged` stream, previously
unused — `ConnectivityChecker` only ever called `checkConnectivity()` once per check before this unit); dev-only
`mocktail`, `bloc_test`. SSE is consumed via a ~30-line hand-rolled parser over `dio`'s existing byte-stream
support, explicitly chosen over any third-party SSE package (research.md R1) — the OpenAPI contract's own
schema for both SSE operations is `content: text/event-stream` / `{type: string}`, i.e. genuinely no typed
shape to generate a client from.

**Storage**: One new on-device store, `ChatLocalCache` (research.md R4) — three independent
`flutter_secure_storage` keys (`chatSessionsLocalCache`, `chatMessagesLocalCache`, `chatLastActiveSessionId`),
same Keychain-backed, JSON-encoded mechanism `EntriesLocalCache` (RF01) already established for personal
content. No local database, no new third-party persistence package.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via
`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
`chat_title_deriver.dart` (pure), `ChatMessage`'s status-transition shape, `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s
silent-refresh-and-retry branches (both the non-streaming shape reused verbatim from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`,
and the new first-frame-only streaming variant, research.md R3), and `ApiClient.sseStream()`'s own frame
parser (a `core/` addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `error_mapper_test.dart`/similar already
live). `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` and `domain_purity_test.dart` both run unmodified against the new
`lib/features/chat/` folder with no exceptions needed.

```text
cerne-ciclo-a/
└── lib/
```

prior unit already established — no deviation. The two `core/network/` additions
(`ApiClient.sseStream()`/`SseFrame`, `ConnectivityChecker.onConnectivityChanged`) live there rather than inside

inside `capture/`). `home/` is extended rather than folded into `chat/` because `home_chat_shell_page.dart`/

rename with no behavioral benefit.

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-rolled SSE parsing in `ApiClient` (research.md R1) | `chat.messages.send`/`.retry` are this app's first and only streaming endpoints; the OpenAPI contract gives them no typed response shape (`text/event-stream`/`{type: string}`) for `call()`'s existing JSON-only path to handle | A third-party SSE package — rejected: introduces a second HTTP-stack assumption alongside `dio`, for a 5-event-type protocol spoken to exactly one backend (research.md R1) |

cache mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own rationale).*

# Cerne — Prototype extract

The visual reference of the product is `cerne-prototype.html` (this folder). Open it in a browser; it needs JavaScript. This extract lists its navigable states, its visual tokens, its components and the implementation notes that come with it.

- **Frame:** 390 × 844 logical points, portrait only, 4 dp grid.
- **Language of the interface:** Portuguese. Every UI text below appears exactly as in the prototype, in quotes.
- **Precedence:** the prototype defines appearance and states. Behavior rules (triggers, timings, filters, error handling) are defined in `docs/input/requirements.md`; where the prototype's simulated behavior differs from a requirement, the requirement prevails.

---

## 1. Navigation map

The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).

```
Splash (auto, 1.8 s)
  └─> Biometria ──tap/error──> PIN inicial / PIN após falha
  │      └─> "usar e-mail e senha" ──> Entrar / criar conta (toggle)
  │                                          └─> submit ──> Home/Chat
  └─(PIN complete, 4 digits)──> Home/Chat
  └─(Face ID/Touch ID ok)──> Home/Chat

Home/Chat (base screen)
  ├─ overlay: Sessão expirada (backend session expires; "Entrar novamente" ──> Biometria)
  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
  └─ overlay: Insertion modal ("+" button) ──> tabs Texto / Áudio / Foto, each with its own sub-states
        (on save, the modal closes and returns to Home/Chat with the record added)

Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
  ├─ overlay: filter sheet ──"Aplicar"──> active filters (chips on the list)
  └─ overlay: export card (download icon) ──> pending ──> processing ──> done | error | empty period

Planos de Ação (base screen, from the side menu) — static screen, 3-column kanban (extension, not implemented)

Configurações (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ dashboard variations: zero entries | one entry | more than 30 (with narrative) | narrative unavailable
  ├─ inline profile-name editing
  ├─ AI persona selection (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) (extension, not implemented)
  ├─ "Sair" ──> Biometria
  └─ overlay: account-deletion confirmation ──"Apagar tudo"──> Biometria (same destination as logout)
```

---

## 2. Navigable states

Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.

| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |

| State | What it shows |
|---|---|

1	# Contract: `EntriesRepository` extension (`lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`)
2	
3	Extends the interface `specs/003-multimodal-capture/contracts/entries-repository.md` already defines
4	(`create`, `cachedEntries`, both unchanged) with the two read methods this unit needs. Still the single seam
5	every feature reading or writing entries depends on — `records/` is simply its first reader.
6	
7	```dart
8	abstract class EntriesRepository {
9	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source}); // unchanged
10	  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                   // unchanged
11	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor});
12	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
13	}
14	```
15	
16	## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` (orchestration, data layer)
17	
18	```dart
19	Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) async {
20	  final result = await _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor);
21	  return result.match(
22	    (failure) => failure is AuthExpiredFailure
23	        ? await _retryAfterSilentRefresh(() => _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor))
24	        : Left(failure),
25	    (page) => Right(page),
26	  );
27	}
28	```
29	
30	## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.getById()` (orchestration, data layer)
31	
32	Identical shape, over `_remoteDataSource.getById(id)` instead.
33	
34	## The shared retry helper (private to `EntriesRepositoryImpl`)
35	
36	```dart
37	Future<Either<Failure, T>> _retryAfterSilentRefresh<T>(
38	  Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function() retry,
39	) async {
40	  final refreshed = await _sessionRepository.refresh();
41	  return refreshed.match(
42	    (_) => Left(const AuthExpiredFailure(message: 'Session could not be renewed', requestId: '')),
43	    (_) => retry(),   // exactly one retry — no loop, no second refresh attempt
44	  );
45	}
46	```
47	
48	- **Exactly one retry.** If the retried call *also* comes back `AuthExpiredFailure` (a pathological
49	  double-expiry), it is returned to the caller as-is — no second refresh attempt, no loop. This is a
50	  deliberately simple, bounded policy; nothing in spec.md requires more.
51	- **The `Left` branch always normalizes to a fresh `AuthExpiredFailure`**, regardless of what the refresh
52	  attempt itself failed with (`AuthInvalidFailure` for no stored refresh token, or whatever `/auth/refresh`
53	  itself returned) — callers (`RecordsBloc`) only ever need to know "could not be silently renewed," not the
54	  refresh call's own internal failure shape, mirroring how `CheckSessionUseCase` (specs/001) already
55	  normalizes every unrenewable-session case down to one outcome rather than leaking the refresh call's raw
56	  failure type upward.
57	- **`create()` is untouched** — out of this unit's scope (research.md R4).
58	
59	## `EntriesRemoteDataSource` additions (data layer)
60	
61	```dart
62	Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) {
63	  return _apiClient
64	      .call('entries-list', method: 'GET', queryParameters: cursor == null ? null : {'cursor': cursor})
65	      .flatMap(_parseEntriesPage);
66	}
67	
68	Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id) {
69	  return _apiClient
70	      .call('entries-get', method: 'GET', pathSegments: [id])
71	      .flatMap(_parseEntry);   // the same private parser create() already uses
72	}
73	```
74	
75	- `_parseEntry` (existing, `create()`'s private parser) is reused verbatim for a single object; a new
76	  `_parseEntriesPage` parses `data` (a list, each element through the same per-entry field logic `_parseEntry`
77	  already has — factored so neither duplicates the other) and `meta.nextCursor`.
78	- Malformed-response parsing failures (`TypeError`/`FormatException`) map to `ValidationFailure`, exactly like
79	  `create()`'s existing `_parseEntry` catch clauses — no new failure-mapping behavior.
80	
81	## `ApiClient.call()` (core layer) — `queryParameters` addition
82	
83	```dart
84	Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
85	  String function, {
86	  required String method,
87	  Map<String, dynamic>? body,
88	  List<String>? pathSegments,
89	  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
90	  AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession,
91	}) async {
92	  // ...unchanged URL-building...
93	  final response = await _dio.request<Map<String, dynamic>>(
94	    url,
95	    data: body,
96	    queryParameters: queryParameters,   // NEW — passed straight through to dio
97	    options: Options(method: method, headers: {...}),
98	  );
99	  // ...unchanged response handling...
100	}
101	```
102	
103	Every existing call site (`entries-create`, `auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) omits the new
104	parameter and is byte-for-byte unaffected.
105	
106	## Who depends on this
107	
108	`RecordsBloc` (`list`/`getById`, via `EntriesRepository` only — never `EntriesRemoteDataSource`/`ApiClient`
109	directly, same layering every existing feature already observes). No other unit yet calls `list()`/`getById()`
110	— RF06 (semantic search) is the next likely caller, reusing the same silent-refresh-and-retry behavior for
111	free.
112	
113	## Test scenarios this contract owns (RNF07/RNF09 — for `/speckit-tasks` to schedule, not built here)
114	
115	| # | Scenario | Expected |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| 1 | `list()` succeeds on the first attempt | `Right(EntriesPage(...))`, no refresh call made |
118	| 2 | `list()` fails `AuthExpiredFailure`, refresh succeeds, retry succeeds | `Right(EntriesPage(...))`, exactly 2 remote calls + 1 refresh call |
119	| 3 | `list()` fails `AuthExpiredFailure`, refresh itself fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, no second refresh attempt |
120	| 4 | `list()` fails any other code (timeout/offline/validation/...) | `Left(<that failure>)` unchanged, no refresh attempted |
121	| 5 | `getById()` — same 4 scenarios as `list()` | same shapes |
122	| 6 | `list(cursor: 'abc')` | `ApiClient.call` receives `queryParameters: {'cursor': 'abc'}` |
123	| 7 | `list()` (no cursor) | `ApiClient.call` receives `queryParameters: null` |
124	| 8 | Response containing a `chat`-sourced entry | Parses without throwing, `EntrySource.chat` |

every feature reading or writing entries depends on — `records/` is simply its first reader.

```dart
abstract class EntriesRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source}); // unchanged
  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                   // unchanged
  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor});
  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
}
```

## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` (orchestration, data layer)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) async {
  final result = await _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor);
  return result.match(
    (failure) => failure is AuthExpiredFailure
        ? await _retryAfterSilentRefresh(() => _remoteDataSource.list(cursor: cursor))
        : Left(failure),
    (page) => Right(page),
  );
}
```

## `EntriesRepositoryImpl.getById()` (orchestration, data layer)

Identical shape, over `_remoteDataSource.getById(id)` instead.

## The shared retry helper (private to `EntriesRepositoryImpl`)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, T>> _retryAfterSilentRefresh<T>(
  Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function() retry,
) async {
  final refreshed = await _sessionRepository.refresh();
  return refreshed.match(
    (_) => Left(const AuthExpiredFailure(message: 'Session could not be renewed', requestId: '')),
    (_) => retry(),   // exactly one retry — no loop, no second refresh attempt
  );
}
```

- **Exactly one retry.** If the retried call *also* comes back `AuthExpiredFailure` (a pathological
  double-expiry), it is returned to the caller as-is — no second refresh attempt, no loop. This is a
  deliberately simple, bounded policy; nothing in spec.md requires more.
- **The `Left` branch always normalizes to a fresh `AuthExpiredFailure`**, regardless of what the refresh
  attempt itself failed with (`AuthInvalidFailure` for no stored refresh token, or whatever `/auth/refresh`
  itself returned) — callers (`RecordsBloc`) only ever need to know "could not be silently renewed," not the
  refresh call's own internal failure shape, mirroring how `CheckSessionUseCase` (specs/001) already
  normalizes every unrenewable-session case down to one outcome rather than leaking the refresh call's raw
  failure type upward.
- **`create()` is untouched** — out of this unit's scope (research.md R4).

## `EntriesRemoteDataSource` additions (data layer)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor}) {
  return _apiClient
      .call('entries-list', method: 'GET', queryParameters: cursor == null ? null : {'cursor': cursor})
      .flatMap(_parseEntriesPage);
}

Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id) {
  return _apiClient
      .call('entries-get', method: 'GET', pathSegments: [id])
      .flatMap(_parseEntry);   // the same private parser create() already uses
}
```

- `_parseEntry` (existing, `create()`'s private parser) is reused verbatim for a single object; a new
  `_parseEntriesPage` parses `data` (a list, each element through the same per-entry field logic `_parseEntry`
  already has — factored so neither duplicates the other) and `meta.nextCursor`.
- Malformed-response parsing failures (`TypeError`/`FormatException`) map to `ValidationFailure`, exactly like
  `create()`'s existing `_parseEntry` catch clauses — no new failure-mapping behavior.

## `ApiClient.call()` (core layer) — `queryParameters` addition

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
  String function, {
  required String method,
  Map<String, dynamic>? body,
  List<String>? pathSegments,
  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
  AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession,
}) async {
  // ...unchanged URL-building...
  final response = await _dio.request<Map<String, dynamic>>(
    url,
    data: body,
    queryParameters: queryParameters,   // NEW — passed straight through to dio
    options: Options(method: method, headers: {...}),
  );
  // ...unchanged response handling...
}
```

Every existing call site (`entries-create`, `auth-session`, `auth-refresh`, `media-ocr`) omits the new
parameter and is byte-for-byte unaffected.

## Who depends on this

`RecordsBloc` (`list`/`getById`, via `EntriesRepository` only — never `EntriesRemoteDataSource`/`ApiClient`
directly, same layering every existing feature already observes). No other unit yet calls `list()`/`getById()`
— RF06 (semantic search) is the next likely caller, reusing the same silent-refresh-and-retry behavior for
free.

## Test scenarios this contract owns (RNF07/RNF09 — for `/speckit-tasks` to schedule, not built here)

| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `list()` succeeds on the first attempt | `Right(EntriesPage(...))`, no refresh call made |
| 2 | `list()` fails `AuthExpiredFailure`, refresh succeeds, retry succeeds | `Right(EntriesPage(...))`, exactly 2 remote calls + 1 refresh call |
| 3 | `list()` fails `AuthExpiredFailure`, refresh itself fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, no second refresh attempt |
| 4 | `list()` fails any other code (timeout/offline/validation/...) | `Left(<that failure>)` unchanged, no refresh attempted |
| 5 | `getById()` — same 4 scenarios as `list()` | same shapes |
| 6 | `list(cursor: 'abc')` | `ApiClient.call` receives `queryParameters: {'cursor': 'abc'}` |
| 7 | `list()` (no cursor) | `ApiClient.call` receives `queryParameters: null` |
| 8 | Response containing a `chat`-sourced entry | Parses without throwing, `EntrySource.chat` |
